lines.text: Something is waking up in the Pacific. And it could break the world's heat record.

phrases.text: Something is waking up in the Pacific.
And it could break the world's heat record.

lines.text: It's called El Niño: when the trade winds weaken, a giant pool of warm water spreads east across the ocean.

phrases.text: a giant pool of warm water spreads east across the ocean.

lines.text: Right now, parts of the Pacific are three degrees hotter than normal. A warm stripe more than 10,000 km long.

phrases.text: Right now, parts of the Pacific are three degrees hotter than normal.

lines.text: Most forecasts say it will become the strongest El Niño ever measured. Even stronger than the "Godzilla" El Niño of 2015.

phrases.text: Most forecasts say it will become the strongest El Niño ever measured.

lines.text: It moves rain around the planet: droughts in Australia and the Amazon, floods in the Americas and East Africa. Crops can fail, and food prices can climb.

lines.text: And on top of global warming, it could make 2027 the hottest year ever recorded. One leading climate scientist puts the odds at 95%.
